one_month_reasoning: The main scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings, estimated for Thu 2026-10-29 before the open (MarketBeat; not yet confirmed on the IR calendar). Consensus is about $4.99 EPS on $10.86B revenue (Alpha Vantage, 21 analysts). Quanta beat by 32% in Q1 and 28% in Q2 and raised guidance both times, so another beat plus a guidance raise or a first 2027 framework is likely. The catch: after the Q2 beat the stock still fell about 15% in five days, as worries about leverage and acquisitions took over. A beat is therefore close to priced in, and the reaction is roughly two-sided. The stock bounced from $634.90 (9/23) to $662.60 after Bernstein's 9/24 upgrade. The 10/1 ex-dividend ($0.11) doesn't matter. I centre the distribution at about $668, a slight upward tilt from beat drift and revisions running 24 up to 0 down over 30 days. Spread is lognormal sigma about 13%: the usual 44%/3.5 = 12.6%, nudged up for the earnings day.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (50%), EV/EBITDA (30%) and FCF yield (20%), all on the next-twelve-months view as of Oct 2027. NTM EPS of about $22.3 x 30x gives $669; NTM EBITDA of $5.4B x 20x less $5.6B net debt gives $672; 2028 FCF of $3.2B at a 3.0% yield gives $700. Blended: about $676.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus x 1.17. Consensus is about 36%/yr over two years (TIKR), and a Substack piece puts the sustainable adjusted EPS CAGR at 15-20% (Capital Blueprint). I used the midpoint, slowing as hyperscaler capex growth is forecast to drop from 54% in 2027 to 12% in 2028 (source 11).

Today it trades at about 34-35x NTM, down from 50x on June 30. Peers: Comfort Systems 31x, EMCOR 22x, MasTec 19x (TIKR). ROIC of 6-8% (Capital Blueprint) argues against a premium to FIX, so I assume modest compression to about FIX's level.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 ~$5.4B x 20x = $108B EV, less ~$5.6B net debt, over 152.4M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $4.15B midpoint, grown about 16% in 2027 (in line with consensus revenue of $45.7B vs $39.6B) and about 14% in 2028, then time-weighted.
$6.1B debt less $0.5B cash at 6/30/26. The $2.0B August notes refinanced commercial paper. I hold it flat on the assumption that FCF is spent on acquisitions.
Today's EV of about $106.6B over NTM EBITDA of about $4.65B is roughly 23x. I apply the same compression as in the P/E method.
$2.25B midpoint compounded at about 19%/yr, in line with EBITDA growth plus margin. A FCF margin of about 6-7% of revenue matches the history in Doroshenko's piece.
The current yield is about 2.1% (2026 FCF midpoint over a $101B market cap). As growth slows I let it normalise toward 3%.

bear.story: Hyperscalers digest AI capex in 2027 (Polymarket gives 35% to a US recession by end-2027), or financing trouble at Oracle or the neoclouds slows data-center power work. Integration problems at the acquired businesses hurt margins. EPS lands at about $19.5 and the multiple falls toward 22x, in line with EMCOR.

base.story: Quanta keeps beating and raising: 2027 EPS of about $20 and NTM EPS of about $22 by late 2027. Labour scarcity supports pricing. The multiple drifts down to about 30-31x.

bull.story: Utility T&D capex above $170B/yr and the more than $1.1T EEI large-load pipeline turn into backlog above $65B. The 'crews are the bottleneck' story (Bernstein) holds, so the premium multiple of about 38x on NTM EPS of $24 comes back.

thesis_break_reason: $470 is about 21x consensus 2027 EPS, roughly EMCOR's multiple. Trading there would most likely mean the growth premium is broken: backlog falling quarter over quarter, a guidance cut, or hyperscaler or utility capex cuts. A 44%-vol name moving with the sector wouldn't normally get that low; it is also below the August low and near the 52-week low of $404.51.

reasoning: Facts: Q2 2026 revenue was $9.56B (+41%), adjusted EPS $4.24, and backlog a record $53.4B. 2026 guidance was raised to $16.45-16.95 EPS and $2.0-2.5B FCF. Consensus is FY26 $16.73 and FY27 $19.77, with 24 upward revisions and none down over 30 days. The stock fell from $720 (6/30) to $635 (9/23) on worries about leverage and acquisitions after the $2B note issue, which compressed the forward P/E from 50x to about 35x, then bounced after Bernstein's upgrade. Alternative signals: (1) Revelio data show active job postings up 52% in 2026 (3,050 vs 2,352) and hiring velocity recovering to about 1,273 per month. ZipRecruiter shows lineman pay of $28-62/hr. Together they point to demand above supply for crews, which backs the labour-bottleneck view. (2) The SupercycleHQ tracker shows trailing hyperscaler capex of $657B, latest quarter up 68-235% YoY, with Alphabet guiding to a 'significant increase' in 2027. Outside forecasts see 2027 capex growth of about 54% and 2028 slowing to 12%, a deceleration the market may start pricing by mid-2027. (3) The EEI large-load list shows more than $1.13T and 71 GW of announced projects (Sept 2026). (4) Retail attention is very low (AltIndex: 0-4 Reddit mentions a month, 33rd percentile vs. peers), so there's no retail froth. (5) Polymarket puts a US recession by end-2027 at 35% (as of 2026-10-02, but on only about $9.7k volume, so a weak signal). The Kobeissi Letter on X cited 33% on an earlier market. (6) Two independent Substacks (Capital Blueprint, Doroshenko) flag a GAAP/adjusted gap of 33-46% and ROIC of 6-8%, which argues against re-rating back to 50x. Valuation blends to about $676, close to spot. Scenarios: 22% bear at $440, 53% base at $690, 25% bull at $920; the mean is about $690. I built the ladder as a lognormal mixture: a wider bear component (sigma 0.35) and tighter base and bull components (sigma 0.22). That gives an overall dispersion of about 38-40%, a bit under the 44% realised vol because backlog visibility is high. P(≥ spot) is about 0.57. Limits: X was not fetched directly, and Google Trends and web-traffic data weren't reachable. Analyst-target data from Twelve Data needs a higher plan; I used the Street mean of about $770 reported by TIKR only as context.
